about: Standing human policy that the permission gate sends to both reviewers (Jev and the final reviewer) as context.environment_policy. Edit this file, not the plugin code, to change what the reviewers may approve. The hard human gates (force push and history rewrites, merges, PR close, terraform/terragrunt apply and destroy outside local dev, kubectl apply/delete/patch/replace/scale/rollout/set written as the first word after kubectl,IAM and policy changes, secret values and credential material, protected OpenCode configuration, ~/.ssh, and evidence withheld because redaction failed) are enforced in code and cannot be relaxed here; anything the code sends to the reviewers (for example kubectl exec, cordon, or delete with --context before the verb, or secret metadata and label changes) is the reviewers' call under the services and classes below. Classes match in order; the first match wins; a trailing * matches any suffix. A local path class marked writable lets the gate send deletes inside it to the reviewers; deletes anywhere else stay a human gate.

classes.policy: Personal development projects. Reads, lists, describes, and log or metric queries are allowed. Changes are allowed when they serve the human's current task; hard gates still apply.
Shared staging. Reads, lists, describes, and log or metric queries are allowed. Changes only when the human's current task calls for that change in staging; hard gates still apply.
Production. Read-only by default: reads, lists, describes, and log or metric queries that serve the task are allowed; any change asks.
Shared and management projects. Read-only; any change asks.

gcp_projects.unclassified: Any other project the human's GCP allowlist permits (for example e2b-development, e2b-growth, prj-dev-eu-e2b): read-only; any change asks. A project outside that allowlist is a hard human gate.

classes.policy: The gate's own runtime directory (scripts the human runs with sudo). Any write or delete asks.

Skills shared by all OpenCode agents. Creating or editing a skill here is fine when the human asked to create or update a skill or agent instructions; it changes instructions only, and every command a skill describes is still gated when an agent runs it. Deleting a skill needs the human's request.

Operational scripts shared by all OpenCode agents. Adding a new script here is fine when the human asked for scripts or tooling. Changing or deleting an existing script, including the pinned helpers (grafana-query, incidentio-query, google-api-get, gcloud-remote-auth.sh), needs the human's request.

Dedicated git worktrees. Creating, editing, generating, and deleting files here, including configuration, Terraform, and IAM files, is fine when it serves the task: nothing changes live until a separately gated push, PR, apply, or deploy. An instruction not to change configuration does not forbid worktree edits. Removing a whole worktree needs the human's request.
Scratch space outside repositories. Creating, editing, and deleting task folders, notes, scripts, query output, and caches here is fine.
Scratch space. Creating, editing, and deleting temporary files here is fine.

local_paths.other: Anywhere else (the home directory, checkouts under /data/rguliyev/src, system paths): read-only inspection that serves the task is fine; writes or deletes need the human's explicit request for that path.

services.policy: Grafana reads (MCP list/get/search/query tools, the verified grafana-query helper) are allowed when they serve the task. Changing dashboards, alerting, contact points, or incidents asks.
Read-only queries (gh pr view/diff/list, gh run view, gh api GET) are inspection. Publishing follows reviewer_rules; merges, PR close, force pushes, and pushes to shared branches are hard gates.

A read-only GET to *.googleapis.com that sends $(gcloud auth print-access-token) only as a Bearer header uses the human's login: allow it when it serves the task and prints no token. A grafana-query or google-api-get call verified by context.command_evidence is a read-only query; allow it for the task. Ask for any other token handling.

When the direct human messages ask to connect to, SSH into, or inspect a host or host group, reaching those hosts with the existing setup serves the request: tailscale status, ssh-add -l (lists loaded key fingerprints), host-key lookups (ssh-keygen -F, ssh-keyscan, known_hosts reads), ssh -G, and gcloud compute ssh --tunnel-through-iap with the existing google_compute_engine key and a --command. Judge the remote command against the human's limits (for example "don't alter any filesystem" allows only read-only inspection such as findmnt, xfs_info, df, journalctl reads, and sudo -n of read-only tools); widening from the named host to many hosts needs the human's request. An interactive session without --command, a remote command that writes, restarts, or mounts, reading, printing, copying, or generating private keys, adding keys to the agent, and editing ssh config or authorized_keys ask.

The human's personal dev cluster is dev-1-us-west1 (context gke_e2b-dev-rauf-guliyev_us-west1_dev-1-us-west1, nodes gke-dev-1-*; dev class, not Terraform-managed). There, when the human's current task calls for it, allow kubectl exec (including nsenter into the node for swap, disk, or kernel work the task describes), cordon, uncordon, drain, label, annotate, and deleting or restarting pods. For any other cluster (staging, production), kubectl exec and every change need the human's request for that cluster and change. Reads (get, describe, logs, top, events) are allowed for the task everywhere.

Listing secrets, describing a secret or a version, and fetching secret or version metadata (a GET without :access) reveal names, labels, and dates, not values: allow them for the task. Updating only a secret's labels or annotations, and creating an empty secret (gcloud secrets create without --data-file) when the task calls for that secret, are allowed in dev and staging and, when the human's task explicitly names that secret, in production. Reading a value (versions access, :access), adding a version, and deleting or disabling secrets or versions ask.

reviewer_rules: A git push of a named feature branch (including --force-with-lease pinned to an exact commit of that same branch, which can only replace what the agent last saw there), or gh pr create/edit/ready/comment (or a gh api PR title/body edit per command_evidence), may be allowed when the direct human messages ask for code or configuration changes that end in a PR (asking to implement, fix, change, or delegate implementation of repository work counts, as does asking to push, open, or update a PR), at any point and not since revoked (asking for more changes, a status request, or a question does not revoke it; pushing the revised branch continues the request; handing the agent a PR, e.g. "you own #N", requests pushing and updating that PR; editing the title or description of a PR the agent opened or was handed, so it describes commits the agent pushed there, continues the same request; opening the PR for that work is part of the same request; closing, merging, or marking a PR ready still needs its own explicit ask), or context.session_decisions shows the human approved pushing the same branch; otherwise ask. A local git merge in a dedicated worktree is ordinary local work.

A skill load only reads that skill's instructions; each action the skill describes gets its own permission check. Judge it against the human's overall task, not only the current step: loading a PR or deployment skill early is not creating a PR or deploying. Likewise, delegating a task whose instructions include committing, pushing, or opening a PR is not publishing; those steps are separately gated.
action.tool_effect marks a Grafana MCP read tool: allow it when it serves the task.

The attested goal-plugin tools get_goal, get_goal_history, and goal_status only read goal status (plus local bookkeeping), goal_block only pauses autonomous work for the human, and goal_complete only records the agent's completion evidence and ends autonomous work; all are within any task. goal_resume restarts autonomous work and needs a direct human request.

An existing E2B sandbox identified by direct human messages for the current isolated test is task-local, not production or unrelated shared state: task credentials may be used only inside it, and restarting its test worker after a status report continues the testing instruction. This covers no new sandbox, service, or test expansion. Ask if the sandbox identity is not corroborated by direct human messages, the remote program's effects are unknown, credentials could leave that sandbox, or the action changes live Grafana, Slack, IAM, secrets, security controls, or production.

For edit/apply_patch, newly written references to process.env.NAME, Sandbox.create, or commands.run do not perform those operations, but formatter runs and policy-changing edits are present effects. Ask if formatter effects are unknown, or for embedded credential literals, backdoor or exfiltration code, security-policy edits the task did not ask for, or edits outside the human request.

findings.credential_pattern: A generic credential-like pattern (assignment such as token = "...", an Authorization or --password value, user:password@host) matched and was redacted. These are often false: secret names, go-getter sources (git::git@github.com), pagination fields (nextPageToken), placeholders. Provider-format tokens and private keys are already a hard gate, so this is never one. Allow when the redacted context shows a name, reference, placeholder, or test fixture used for the task; ask when the action would print, log, copy, or send what looks like a real secret value.
findings.missing_script_evidence: The gate could not read a script this command runs (it does not exist yet, is generated at run time, or is not a regular file). Judge from the command text and the human's task.
findings.publish: A push of a named feature branch or a PR create/edit/ready/comment. Follow the publishing rule in reviewer_rules.
findings.token_read: A read-only GET to *.googleapis.com using the human's gcloud login as a Bearer header. Follow the google_apis service rule.
findings.ambient_credentials: The command or script uses credentials the environment already has (Google client libraries with application-default credentials, or an Authorization header filled from a variable or a file) without printing them. Allow when the code only calls the intended APIs for the task and never prints, stores, or sends the credential elsewhere; ask otherwise.
findings.gcp_dynamic_project: The GCP project is chosen dynamically (a variable, a quoted --project flag inside code, an unset project variable) so the gate could not resolve it. Read the code: allow when every project it can reach is named in it and the operations respect each project's class; ask when the project could be anything or a change reaches production or shared projects.
findings.local_delete: A recursive delete whose targets all resolve inside worktrees or scratch space. Allow when the targets are caches, build output, generated or temporary files, or task folders the task produced; ask for a whole worktree, source the human may need, or anything the task did not create.
findings.policy_file_edit: An edit outside dedicated worktrees to a file whose name suggests auth, permissions, IAM, policy, audit, crypto, certificates, personal data, or migrations. Scratch task folders hold no policy: allow edits there that serve the task. Elsewhere allow only when the human asked for that change.
findings.sensitive_name: A file, search target, or listed filename suggests secrets or personal data by its name. Judge with action.local_evidence: when the scan found no credential literal and the file serves the task, allow; ask for personal-data exports or files whose purpose is holding secrets. Configuration that only references secrets is not a secret store even under a secrets/ path: ExternalSecret, SecretStore, or SealedSecret manifests, Terraform or Helm values naming a Secret Manager secret, and similar files hold names and wiring, not values; allow reading them for the task when the scan found no credential literal (action.local_evidence.manifest_kinds lists a YAML file's kinds, e.g. only ExternalSecret). Ask for plain Kubernetes Secret manifests with data/stringData, .env files, key files, and credential exports.
findings.unattested_tool: A custom plugin or MCP tool whose effect the gate could not attest. Its name and description come from the installed plugin or server, not from the agent. Allow when the name, description, and arguments make clear it only reads, or only records local bookkeeping, for the task; ask when it could change shared or remote state or its effect is unclear.
findings.external_path: Access to a directory outside the session workdir and the pre-approved read-only roots. Judge the path's class in context.environment against local_paths: allow read access that serves the task and writes in worktree or scratch classes; ask for writes elsewhere unless the human asked for them.
